content.text:
I think the sample contains Ca2LaTaO6 (mp-1227477) as the main phase plus Ca2CuIrO6 (mvc-5634), but the fit is only fair, so confidence is moderate.

- **Main phase:** Ca2LaTaO6 is the only candidate that fits on its own (R-factor 0.73). Each of the other single-phase fits I ran stayed between 0.96 and 0.97.
- **Second phase:** After fitting Ca2LaTaO6, the residual still shows peaks near 19.9–20.6° and around 32°. Adding Ca2CuIrO6 removes the 20° peaks and most of the 32° peak, and lowers R to 0.65.
- **Close alternative:** SrCaMnGaO5 (mp-1218355) as the second phase gives nearly the same R (0.66), but it leaves the 20° peaks unexplained. A three-phase fit improves R only slightly, to 0.64.
- **Why confidence is limited:** Ca2LaTaO6 underestimates the strong peak pair at about 18.5/19.05°. Its main peak near 31° is also slightly mispositioned, which shows as a negative residual just below it. The baseline noise also inflates every R-factor here.
